- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +3% above recent high.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates by 0.5–1.5% in early days (1–7) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% to first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.33” or “0.67” alternation, model exhibits oscillation bias; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values before applying trend.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >2% for 3 consecutive days, model is lagging; adjust forecast to match recent 3-day average + 0.5% buffer.
